view: The CEO exit has happened and is in the price; the governance story is now about whether legal exposure moves from Megaspeed/Alice Huang to Nvidia itself (TB1) and whether Commerce turns its draft Southeast Asia rules into a material restriction (TB3). I would keep TB2 as fired and buying paused until the owner rules. TB1, TB3 and TB4 have not fired, and TB4 is not even on watch. The next two weeks hold two binary events (the 2026-11-17 print and the Huang briefing reported for 2026-11-18), so I see a roughly even split between up and down, with less weight on range than the base rate.

evidence.point: The 8-K says Huang resigned as President, CEO and director effective immediately (accepted 2026-11-11). It gives no reason and reports no disagreement. Kress is interim CEO and stays CFO, Harvey C. Jones is Chair, and a permanent-CEO search is open. 'No disagreement' is standard 8-K wording and does not answer whether the exit came under legal pressure.

Congress: three House chairs (Mast, Moolenaar, Crawford) asked Huang personally for a closed-door briefing on 2026-11-18. The request is voluntary, not a subpoena. CNBC says he agreed to testify before Thanksgiving. The scrutiny is aimed at the individual, which supports the reading that the exit came under regulatory pressure (TB2). Because the session is closed-door, live headlines should be fewer than from a televised hearing.

No charges against Huang, Nvidia, Megaspeed or Alice Huang. Megaspeed (statement on 2026-11-15) says Alice Huang left on 2025-08-30, that it has hired outside counsel for an internal investigation, and that it denies wrongdoing. Bloomberg reports that a Chinese company founded by Alice Huang obtained banned Nvidia chips through Dell and Super Micro servers. That is diversion through OEM channels, not a finding against Nvidia, so TB1 has not fired.

WSJ: Megaspeed arranged about $12B of Nvidia chip shipments to Chinese companies between Mar 2024 and Jun 2025, though the documents do not establish delivery. Commerce is developing rules for Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore, and Malaysia is investigating re-exports. Nvidia's China revenue was $12.4B in the six months to Jul 26. This is the main path to TB3, but nothing has been enacted.

NYT: officials disagree. Lutnick favours narrower controls (seven countries, future shipments only, notification rather than licensing for some Chinese training). Others favour worldwide restrictions. The outcome ranges from immaterial to a TB3-grade cut, and a split administration usually means delay, which lowers my 2w TB3 odds.

FT: a shareholder class action has been filed against Nvidia and Huang. D&O cover is Side A only (up to $900M), so corporate defence costs and damages may be uninsured. This is a slow-burn cost and not a thesis break. Class actions routinely follow large drops, so I treat it as noise for 2w and a small negative for 2q.

Sell-side capitulation: at least six downgrades on Thu-Fri (HSBC to Hold, target 170), Ives target cut from 300 to 225 (still Buy), and six straight weekly declines, the longest since Oct 2012. Analyst actions count as one evidence group. After a key-person shock, downgrades usually lag the price and do not lead it.

Holds rose from 9 to 15 since 2026-11-12, and the average target fell from 309.21 to 286.12 (low 170). Fwd P/E on next FY is 17.51 and last-quarter revenue grew 105.9% YoY. The governance de-rating has happened while the earnings base has not been touched, which is why my next_quarter call stays above the down bucket.

How the market priced the shock: Nov 12 opened at 151.005 on the exit, hit a low of 148.80 and closed at 166.19 on 747.7M shares. Fri Nov 13 opened at 169.905 (high 170.00), fell to a low of 158.39 and closed at 162.85, giving back the rebound. The first reaction was absorption, then a second wave of selling as the Megaspeed, downgrade and class-action stories arrived. That fits how key-person shocks usually play out: a gap, a relief bounce, then a grind while follow-on news lands.
Week: NVDA -14.78% vs SOX +6.86%, AMD +20.17%, AVGO +11.53%, SPX +2.49%. The damage is company-specific and does not point to an AI-demand break. That is consistent with TB4 not firing.

what_would_change_my_mind: Expected (not a trigger): the 2026-11-17 print happens. What matters is (a) any new legal-proceedings or risk-factor language on DOJ, BIS, Megaspeed or Southeast Asia channels in the release or 10-Q, and (b) whether Kress or Chair Jones gives a reason for the resignation or a CEO-search timeline. Beat or miss size belongs to fundamentals.

Expected (not a trigger): the Huang closed-door briefing (reported for 2026-11-18, voluntary). The outcome trigger is a credible report that he said Nvidia knew of the diversion, which would raise TB1 sharply. A briefing with no new disclosure lowers the governance risk premium.
TB1 fires: any DOJ or Commerce charge, settlement, penalty or company admission that Nvidia itself (not only Megaspeed, Alice Huang or the OEMs) violated export controls, before 2027-03-31.

TB3 fires: Commerce publishes or enacts the Malaysia/Indonesia/Singapore rule (or a worldwide version) in a form that materially cuts addressable market, i.e. it covers existing remote-access or cloud channels and requires licensing rather than notification, before 2027-03-31. The narrower Lutnick version would NOT fire TB3 on my reading.

TB2 un-pause case (owner's decision): the board or its investigation states the resignation was unrelated to the export or Megaspeed matter, AND the briefing and 10-Q add no Nvidia-level legal exposure, AND a permanent CEO is named or a credible timeline is given.
TB4 WATCH: two or more of MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/META show last-quarter run-rate more than 10% below TTM, or any one of them guides capex down on its next call. TB4 fires only if two or more guide down.

More bearish on price: a daily close below 148.80 before 2026-11-27 (about -8.6%, reachable within the 2w -5%/-10% window range). More bullish: a daily close above 179.92 before 2026-12-31 (about +10.5%, reachable at the 6w +10% rate of 54.7%).
notes_for_chair: TB STATUS: TB1 NOT fired. TB2 FIRED per the chair's 2026-11-12 ruling, awaiting the owner's confirmation; I recommend keeping it fired. TB3 NOT fired. TB4 NOT fired and NOT on watch (0/4 falling).

TB2 re-check with new facts. FOR fired: an immediate exit that also gave up the board seat, no reason given, and Congress now seeking Huang personally while a diversion story links Megaspeed and Alice Huang. AGAINST: still no charges against anyone, the briefing is voluntary, and the 8-K reports no disagreement. Nothing in the last 3 days resolves the question in either direction. Keeping the pause costs little, while unpausing too early could mean buying into the briefing and a possible TB1. Re-check points: after the 2026-11-17 print and 10-Q, and after the 2026-11-18 briefing.

TB odds (my judgment, not slice numbers). TB1: 2w ~3%, 2q ~18% (was 4%/20%). Bloomberg and WSJ point to OEM and channel diversion with no charges, and DOJ/Commerce enforcement takes a long time; the uninsured D&O structure raises the cost if it does fire. TB3: 2w ~4%, 2q ~25% for a MATERIAL rule (about 45% for some rule being published). Commerce is drafting, but the administration is split (NYT), which usually delays and narrows. TB4: 2w ~1%, 2q ~6%. Capex run-rates are 16-44% above TTM, and the next guidance points are the hyperscalers' next quarterly calls (dates not in slice).

How these shocks usually price: a key-person exit gaps down, partly retraces as the 'when does it happen' uncertainty clears, then drifts on follow-on headlines until successor clarity arrives. Regulatory overhangs are priced in steps at each official document (rule text, charge, settlement), and a final settlement or rule often marks the low because it ends the uncertainty. The Nov 12-13 sequence matches the first two steps. The step that matters next is an official document, not commentary.

Noise, next 2 weeks: senators' statements, the reinstatement petition (135k signatures), Trump suggesting Tim Cook, candidate-name speculation, further downgrades or target cuts, the class action itself, Megaspeed or China denials. Signal, next 2 weeks: credible accounts of what Huang told the committee, 10-Q legal-proceedings language, any DOJ or Commerce filing, a board statement on the resignation reason, further senior-executive departures, and Commerce rule text being published.

Noise, next 2 quarters: the lobbying back-and-forth on control scope, and analyst re-ratings. Signal, next 2 quarters: the permanent-CEO appointment and who it is (an outsider without Nvidia customer relationships is a bigger strategic change than an insider), the outcome of the board investigation, the scope of the final Commerce rule, the Malaysia re-export findings, and hyperscaler capex guidance on their next calls.

Before vs after the 2026-11-17 print: before, my view is governance-driven and two-sided with a fat down tail. After, I would shift 2w odds by up to about 10 points toward whichever side the disclosures support. A clean 10-Q legal section plus an uneventful briefing would move me toward 40/31/29. New legal language or a reported admission would move me toward 28/27/45 and raise TB1 to ~30% over 2q.

Measurement note: the 2w bucket is scored at the 2026-11-27 close, which is the half-day session after Thanksgiving, and the window now includes both the print and the briefing. Changes vs my 2026-11-12 submission (price 164.33, older thresholds): 2w 33/27/40 -> 35/31/34, this quarter 32/34/34 -> 33/35/32, next quarter 40/28/32 -> 41/28/31, confidence 50 -> 48. Reasons: no charges after 3 days, a closed-door rather than public hearing, and the exit low held. Lower confidence because options positioning is still deferred.

Cross-domain: the D&O Side A-only exposure and any 10-Q contingency belong to fundamentals. Peer outperformance (AMD +20.17% w) as a share-shift question belongs to relative_strength. Stale AAII/CNN pages belong to sentiment. Options positioning is deferred.

Pre-mortem: if this is badly wrong in 3 months, the most likely reason is that a clean print plus a non-event briefing let the market re-rate a stock at 17.5x forward earnings quickly, so the TB2 pause cost entries near the 148.80 low. The second most likely reason is that Commerce published a broad worldwide rule faster than the split administration suggested.
